title: Wayland: Editor crash on start with prefer_wayland=true only if editor window was not maximized or resized on last use
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in: 4.6.1-rc1, 4.6
Not reproducible in: 4.5

### System information

Godot v4.6.1.rc1.mono - Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS 24.04 on Wayland - Wayland display driver, Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT (RADV GFX1201) - AMD Ryzen 9 9950X 16-Core Processor (32 threads) - 62.37 GiB memory

### Issue description

This only applies with prefer_wayland = true while using Wayland and while the editor window is *not* maximized.

When using the editor in a non-maximized mode everything functions normally on first run.  When you close the editor and start it again, during initialization it shows a much smaller window and then starts an editor session with a different sized window than the previous run.

If you now close the editor window again and restart the editor, it yields a 100% crash trying to create an invalid swap chain with this output:

```
Godot Engine v4.6.1.rc1.mono.official.7bfffc846 - https://godotengine.org
WARNING: Can't obtain the XDG decoration manager. Libdecor will be used for drawing CSDs, if available.
     at: init (platform/linuxbsd/wayland/wayland_thread.cpp:4850)
WARNING: xdg-toplevel-icon protocol not found! Cannot set window icon.
     at: init (platform/linuxbsd/wayland/wayland_thread.cpp:4857)
WARNING: FIFO protocol not found! Frame pacing will be degraded.
     at: init (platform/linuxbsd/wayland/wayland_thread.cpp:4872)
WARNING: radv is not a conformant Vulkan implementation, testing use only.
Vulkan 1.4.328 - Forward+ - Using Device #0: AMD - AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT (RADV GFX1201)

ERROR: Condition "err != VK_SUCCESS" is true. Returning: ERR_CANT_CREATE
   at: swap_chain_resize (drivers/vulkan/rendering_device_driver_vulkan.cpp:3369)
ERROR: Wayland protocol error 0 on interface wp_viewport@45.
   at: _poll_events_thread (platform/linuxbsd/wayland/wayland_thread.cpp:3349)
Signal: SIGILL (signal SIGILL: illegal operand)
```

Disabling prefer_wayland in the editor_settings-4.6.tres is the only way to start the editor again.

This crash has two 100% workarounds I have found while still using prefer_wayland=true:

1. Run the editor maximized.  There are no issues on future runs that remain maximized.
2. Resize the editor window every single time you run.  On the next restart, it will show an incorrectly sized window again and start an editor session with a different sized window.  If you keep resizing the window at least once every editor session, then the crash never happens on subsequent runs.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run 4.6 or 4.6.1-rc1 editor on a Linux using Wayland.
2. Create an empty project.  Add nothing to the project.
3. In the editor settings, set Prefer Wayland to true/enabled.  Save and restart.
4. After the editor starts again, ensure the editor window is not maximized and close the editor window.
5. Start the editor again.  Notice during startup the window size is different.
6. Close the editor again
7. Restart the editor once more and it should crash.
8. To start the editor again, edit ~/.config/editor_settings-4.6.tres and set prefer_wayland to false

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

N/A
